title: In a composite of two morphisms, if two of the three are universal homeomorphisms then so is the third
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a morphism presented as a composite of two morphisms, if any two of the three morphisms involved are universal homeomorphisms then so is the third (statement lines 11433-11439). The counted proof treats the three possible pairs: the easy case is closure under composition, the case of the composite and the first factor follows by base changing to the target and using the two-out-of-three property for homeomorphisms, and the remaining case requires base changing to the middle scheme and analysing an auxiliary morphism defined by the universal property of fibre products, which is shown to be a bijective closed immersion because the relevant base changed morphism is a homeomorphism, hence affine and separated (proof lines 11441-11488). It is H2: all three cases are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard closure, affineness and immersion statements.
